Subject: Capacity planning for Private deployment — lead times and pool sizing

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Polaris is excited about Redwood's Private offering. We're starting to pull together an internal MAP and need sharper answers on two things before we lock timings with procurement:

1) Typical lead times for Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) when we commit to a GPU pool (H100s vs A100s).
2) Sizing scenarios for a 6–12 month runway (throughput targets: 10k tokens/sec steady, burst to 40k).

Can you share an initial staging-to-activation timeline we can include in our MAP? Tom (cc) is our infra lead and will drive sizing decisions.

Also, send whatever templates/checklists you have for acceptance criteria and canary rollout.

Best,
Alice

Subject: Re: Capacity planning for Private deployment — lead times and pool sizing

Hi Alice / Tom —

Really appreciate the clear ask. I sketched an initial MAP-focused timeline and three sizing scenarios for the MAP document attached. High level:

- Timeline summary (staging -> activation):
  • Eval & benchmark window: 2–4 weeks (pilot on hosted or short-lived private cluster)
  • Staging acceptance and security review: 3–5 weeks (SOC2 evidence, network tests)
  • Procurement & provisioning lead time: 8–14 weeks for Reserved Dedicated (cloud provider + racks), 10–18 weeks for Private on-prem (hardware + KMS/HSM integrations)
  • Activation & canary: 1–2 weeks once infra is provisioned

- Sizing scenarios (tokens/sec):
  • Base (10k steady): 8x A100 or 4x H100 equivalent (quantized run)
  • Growth (20k steady, 40k burst): 16x A100 or 8x H100
  • Aggressive (40k steady): 32+ A100 or 16+ H100 — recommend split across tranches to avoid long lead-time waits

Attached: MAP-draft-polaris-v1.pdf — includes milestone dates, acceptance criteria checklist, and a mutual action milestones table.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Internal alignment on preferred GPU types and acceptable quantization/latency trade-offs (Tom + infra).
2) Quick SOC2 evidence handshake — I'll drop our standard appendix.
3) Confirm target activation quarter so I can align procurement windows and propose tranche dates.

I'll loop in Karthik for technical sizing notes.

Cheers,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical notes to feed into the MAP. Quoting Priyom below.

> Sizing scenarios (tokens/sec):

A few concrete considerations that change tranches:
- Quantization: 4-bit + QKV optimizations reduce H100-equivalent footprint by ~30% for our Llama-family runs; if Polaris is comfortable with quantization, you can reduce physical GPU count.
- Sequence length profile: numbers above assume avg seq len ~256. If you have longer sequences (>=1024) a single H100 supports fewer concurrent sessions and pool sizing needs to increase ~1.6x.
- KV cache persistence: for Private, enabling persistent KV cache across requests reduces burst compute but raises state/storage requirements in staging.

Suggested tranche plan (to reduce procurement lead risk):
• Tranche A (Pilot): 2 H100s + 4 A100s (for benchmarking + canary) — get this within 8–10 weeks.
• Tranche B (Scale to base): additional 6 A100s or 2 H100s (arrive in next 8 weeks).
• Tranche C (Buffer for peak): procure as optional add-on after 12 weeks if usage trends justify.

I'll also prepare a short acceptance-run checklist (latency P50/P95 targets, tail latency, cost per token envelope) and share as a follow-up.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity planning for Private deployment — lead times and pool sizing

Alice / Team —

Thanks — this is great progress. I pulled the technical notes into a condensed MAP milestone table and attached a working schedule (Polaris-MAP-schedule.xlsx) so procurement can see tentative PO windows. Key milestones we recommend for inclusion in Polaris' MAP:

- Week 0: MAP kickoff + scope sign-off (define models, SLAs, security scope)
- Weeks 1–4: Eval & pilot (Tranche A) — run canonical workloads, perf regressions, and initial security scans
- Weeks 5–9: Staging acceptance + SOC2 evidence exchange (we will provide a SOC2 appendix; expect customer evidence requests to take up to 2 weeks)
- Weeks 10–18: Procurement & hardware delivery (target separate PO lines for tranche B to shorten lead risk)
- Weeks 19–20: Activation & canary (slos validated, traffic ramp to 20% -> 100%)

Acceptance criteria (short):
- Latency: P50 <= 75ms, P95 <= 250ms for 256 seq on H100 quantized profile
- Functional: end-to-end inference with KV persistence and rollout/lifecycle hooks
- Security: KMS integration verified, audit logs streaming to Polaris SIEM

Attachments included: Polaris-MAP-schedule.xlsx; SOC2-evidence.zip (redacted sample docs).

Operational asks for Polaris team:
1) Confirm whether you prefer H100-primary or A100-primary runs (this drives procurement cadence).
2) Confirm budget quarter for activation so we can propose tranche PO windows tied to hardware lead times.

We'll keep the MAP as a living doc; once you confirm preference I'll translate to a formal mutual action table and deliver a SOW draft (procurement-ready).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
